key_insight: Gaussian process PDE solvers can enforce linear inequality constraints by conditioning sequentially on equality information first and then on a finite-dimensional inequality event, yielding a valid non-Gaussian posterior.
engineering_relevance: This lets practitioners encode admissibility requirements like nonnegativity, monotonicity, and no-arbitrage directly into probabilistic PDE solvers without changing the underlying physics-informed conditioning step.
method: Condition a GP prior on PDE residuals, boundary data, and measurements to obtain a physics-informed posterior.
Use that posterior as the prior for a virtual-point inequality update via truncated-Gaussian moments.
Interpret the probability of the noisy constraint event as a measure of agreement with the specified bounds.
evidence_signal: On a Poisson benchmark, an added monotonicity constraint reduced reconstruction error by 63%; on a thinned S&P 500 option chain, no-arbitrage constraints cut held-out extrapolation error by 22% and reduced calendar-arbitrage violations from 10% to 1%; on air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a sub-zero-tail proxy by 74% at the sparsest monitor count.
watch_item: The inequality update is non-Gaussian and depends on finite virtual points, so scalability and constraint placement may affect accuracy and computational cost.
paper_title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
